text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: Elevated packet loss and intermittent BGP path oscillation to us-west-2 via CarrierQ (AS12345). Auto-paging oncall. Root cause suspected: upstream transit instability affecting TCP flows and DNS resolution for a subset of prefixes. Please ack and coordinate.

soren: acked. I'm on-call for network. seeing ~9-18% packet loss to a handful of /24s in us-west-2, spikes every 30-90s. latency normal between spikes. paging team and starting triage.

maya: joining. on-call routing snapshot shows flapping AS path lengths, multiple withdraws then re-advertise from CarrierQ. Also seeing increased BGP RIB churn on our peering with CarrierQ. Will paste outputs.

maya: ```
# show bgp neighbors 203.0.113.2 advertised-routes | tail -n 30
* 203.0.113.2       12345    0        00:02:14   1200 prefixes (origins)
# show route 198.51.100.0/24
Paths: (2 available)
  Advertised to update-group 0
  0 12345 65010 i
    from 203.0.113.2 (203.0.113.2)
     rx 2026-03-15 08:12:34
  0 64512 65010 i
    from 198.51.100.1 (198.51.100.1)
     rx 2026-03-15 08:11:58
``` 

maya: traceroute from our edge -> target shows TCP retransmits and occasional TTL drop in transit.

jamie: @soren @maya can we failover to alt-transit (CloudRing) for affected prefixes? We have backup export policies but need to ensure no blackholes. Also customers are reporting API timeouts in us-west. What's the blast radius?

chris: customer-success: just got an inbound from a midmarket customer in us-west experiencing 502s and retry storms. They said it's intermittent starting ~08:10 PDT. Impacted services: real-time indexing and a small subset of API keys pinned to us-west nodes.

soren: assessment: roughly 6 customer-facing prefixes (small subset) are seeing >5% packet loss which causes http connection resets. Not global, mostly us-west AZs in one colo fed via CarrierQ. Severity: P2 — sustained user impact on some customers.

netops: opened ticket with CarrierQ: #CQ-452891. They acknowledge elevated errors on peering fabric and report 'micro-flaps' during edge maintenance window. ETA unknown. We're asking for immediate mitigation and community to withdraw problematic announcements.

maya: mitigation plan:
- short-term: shift affected prefixes to CloudRing by raising preference via BGP localpref on our edge for those prefixes (no customer config change). Apply prepends/communities if CloudRing needs.
- mid-term: enable selective prefix failover (route-map match list -> set local-preference 200) on our transit-facing routers.
- long-term: coordinate scheduled migration of those prefixes off CarrierQ.

jamie: live commands I'm proposing (apply on rtr-edge1/rtr-edge2):
```bash
configure terminal
route-map FAILOVER-CARRIERQ permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list AFFECTED-PRFX
 set local-preference 200
exit
ip prefix-list AFFECTED-PRFX seq 5 permit 198.51.100.0/24
router bgp 65010
 neighbor 198.51.100.1 route-map FAILOVER-CARRIERQ in
end
write memory
```

soren: good. I'll schedule the route-map rollout. Two-step: apply on rtr-edge1 only, monitor for 2 mins, then rtr-edge2. Need someone to watch customer errors and DNS behavior.

chris: I'll coordinate with customer-success: will notify impacted customers with a short blurb and ETA for mitigation. Draft: "We are experiencing intermittent connectivity to us-west. We're failing traffic to an alternate transit provider; some requests may still see retries for a short window. We'll update in 15 minutes." ok?

customer-success: ok send now. Add contact link to status page and note that keys pinned to us-west may need to retry.

maya: rolling on rtr-edge1 now (applying route-map). watching BGP table.

maya: rtr-edge1: route-map in place. BGP now prefers path via CloudRing for 198.51.100.0/24. packet loss samples dropping from 12% -> ~2% on that prefix.

soren: rtr-edge2 rollout in 30s.

maya: rtr-edge2 applied. both edges show localpref 200 to CloudRing for affected prefixes. BGP AS path stabilized. Packet loss now within normal bounds for most prefixes.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: ACTION: Mitigation applied - prefix failover to CloudRing. Please update incident timeline and schedule postmortem. If CarrierQ reports resolution, we'll coordinate a controlled reintroduce.

netops: CarrierQ updated ticket: they had a misconfigured maintenance job that accidentally caused flap storm when modifying interface stack. They're rolling a fix to the fabric. We have asked for commit NOT to reintroduce flaps and to notify us before clear.

jamie: next steps: keep monitoring for 60m, capture pcap on the edges for the period 08:06-08:42, collect bgp updates (/var/log/bgp-updates.log snippet), and prepare changelog for customers. Will schedule 2-hour postmortem once stable.

soren: handoff: I'm going offline for 30m at 09:00PT. @maya will be the primary owner during that window. If anything escalates, page oncall again with urgency.

maya: acked. I'll keep 10m check-ins and update the incident channel with metrics.

chris: customers notified. monitoring dashboards show request error rate for affected hosts falling back to baseline.

customer-success: thanks team. customers appreciate the rapid failover. keep an eye on DNS TTL churn — we saw a few cached entries during the flap.

soren: incident status: mitigated -> degraded. Moving to monitoring/observe. Will open postmortem and include timeline, BGP dumps, CarrierQ ticket, and mitigation commands.

incident-bot: :page_with_curl: Incident status updated to MITIGATED (degraded). Incident owner: maya. Postmortem requested. Closing non-critical pages.
